rows.method_summary: Dictionary encoding keeps original complete values once and replaces repeated values with explicit integer indices. Shared dictionaries and indices travel together. This is a representation reference; no Arrow runtime dependency, binary format or new Store is introduced.
rows.application: Initial Qwen-tokenized two-record engineering fixtures omitted one selected old revision after binding sharing. Extend the generic reversible dictionary principle to repeated record IDs, exact repeated nonempty scope objects and explicit read-more references. Preserve complete actual values, body slices, source role/hash, historical/current labels and missing/partial coverage.
limitations: JSON dictionaries can increase cost on small packets; tables and explanation count toward actual2048 Qwen-token budget.
Model interpretation and semantic benefit remain unverified; representation savings are not formal effectiveness or speedup.
No query/rank/threshold/source-selection change, new dependency/service, deployment, SDK upgrade or benchmark/gold access.

rows.read_scope: Six exact-pin reference files, installed metadata and file hash map; not a full project reproduction.
summary: Actual sync add infer=True dispatches additive extraction through VllmLLM.generate_response and patched client.chat.completions.create.
Extraction transport exceptions raise LLMError; JSON parse errors can instead lead to an empty actual native result. Empty result is not proof of valid semantic no_change.
Public get_all filters owner, defaults top_k20/show_expired false and bounds internal fetch; absence of a returned card is not a full-bank absence proof.
Public get(id) and history(id) are not owner-filtered APIs; reader must establish actual owned ID before calling history/delivering get output.
Native history exposes actual entry IDs, old/new memory, event and timestamps. It does not expose MiLAi integer revisions or candidate CAS.
Snapshot must occur before close. Source inspection does not demonstrate actual independent same-path reopen or four-arm shared cap enforcement.
